content.title: About
content.content: Barbecue beef with sauce is made from selected cuts of beef marinated in aromatic spices and a sweet‑tangy tomato‑based sauce, then slowly baked until tender. The product is ready to eat: simply heat and serve as a main dish or use in salads, sandwiches, and pastas.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The classic barbecue recipe originates from the southern United States, where meat was traditionally cooked over open fire.
The sauce combines tomato paste, brown sugar, vinegar, and smoky spices, giving it a distinctive sweet‑sour flavor.
The beef used is typically from the rib or chuck, cuts rich in connective tissue that become especially juicy after long simmering.
When stored properly in the refrigerator, the product retains its flavor for up to 7 days.
Some versions add a dash of liquid smoke to enhance the smoky aroma.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Beef provides all essential amino acids needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Iron and zinc
items.content: Red meat is a good source of heme iron and zinc, supporting immune function and metabolism.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, important for the nervous system and energy production.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: The product fits low‑carb diets as it contains virtually no sugar.

items.title: Antioxidant content
items.content: Spices and tomato sauce provide antioxidants that help protect cells.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beef.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: The sauce can be salty; people with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: Beef contains saturated fats, so moderate consumption is advised for heart‑related conditions.

items.title: Heat treatment
items.content: The product must be heated to an internal temperature of 75 °C to eliminate food‑borne risks.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the product in a microwave or skillet until hot. Serve with vegetables, mashed potatoes, or use as a filling for burgers and tacos. Fresh herbs or a squeeze of lime can brighten the flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C in the original packaging or an airtight container. Once opened, keep for up to 5 days. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C; fully thaw and reheat before consumption.
